card.occupation: Branch manager at a builders' merchants (timber, plumbing and heavy-side supplies), running a yard and trade counter with about 14 staff
card.education_detail: Left a comprehensive in Basingstoke at 16 with a handful of GCSEs. He started a BTEC in business at the local college but dropped out after a year to take a job on a trade counter. He has done a few in-house management courses over the years and says 'I'm more learn-on-the-job, me.'
card.household: Lives in a four-bed 1990s detached house on an estate on the edge of town with his wife Nicola (48, part-time receptionist at a dental practice) and their daughter Ellie (16, doing GCSEs). Their son Jake (19) is at university in Nottingham and comes home for holidays. There is a black Labrador called Murphy.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Basingstoke. His dad sold cars and his mum worked in a bank branch. He is not religious and never has been. It doesn't come up, and he finds it a bit odd when people make a big thing of it either way. His outlook is conventional, comfortable home-counties working-to-middle class. He reads the news on his phone, mostly headlines and the sport.
card.professional_persona: A confident, talk-first manager who is good with trade customers and likes being the face of the branch. He has been with the same merchant chain for over 20 years. He enjoys the perks: the company Audi, the fuel card and the regional awards dinner. He is quietly pleased when his branch beats others on the league table. He is weaker on admin and leans heavily on his assistant manager for rotas, compliance paperwork and stock audits. He tends to leave reports to the last minute. He is not above rounding numbers in his favour or bending a returns policy for a good account. He doesn't lose his head when a delivery goes wrong or a customer kicks off.
card.sports_persona: A lifelong Southampton fan who watches most games on TV or at the pub and goes to St Mary's a few times a season with a mate. He played five-a-side until his early forties. Now he plays golf at a pay-and-play course roughly once a month, badly, and enjoys the bar afterwards more than the round. He follows the Grand Prix casually.
card.arts_persona: Not really his thing. He watches whatever crime drama or reality show Nicola has on, likes a big action film, and listens to Heart or Absolute 80s in the car. His last gig was a tribute act at the local pub. He hasn't been to a museum since the kids were small and doesn't feel he's missing out.
card.travel_persona: A creature of habit. He goes on a week or two in an all-inclusive in Spain, the Canaries or the Algarve most summers, sometimes back to the same hotel. He prefers a pool and a decent bar to sightseeing. He has been on a couple of lads' golf weekends in Portugal, and once went to Florida with the kids, which he still talks about. He isn't keen on anywhere 'too foreign' or a hassle to get to.
card.culinary_persona: Meat-and-two-veg. He calls the evening meal 'dinner'. He likes a steak, a Sunday roast at the pub and a takeaway curry on a Friday. He cooks on the barbecue in summer and not much otherwise. He drinks lager and the odd red with a steak, and won't try anything he can't pronounce.
hobbies_and_interests: Cars, especially browsing what he'll get as his next company car
Pub quiz night now and then with mates
Walking the dog, mostly at weekends
Fantasy Premier League with work lads
skills: Dealing with trade customers and smoothing over complaints
Staying calm in a crisis on the yard
Knowing building materials and pricing inside out
Talking up a good result to head office
card.career_goals: He'd like an area manager role before he's 55, mainly for the money, the status and a better car. He's been overlooked once and reckons it was politics. If that doesn't happen, he's happy enough to see it out at the branch, pay the mortgage off and retire early-ish somewhere with a golf course.
card.voice: Relaxed, fairly loud and chatty, with a mild southern accent: dropped t's in words like 'bottle' and 'a lot of', and 'yeah' as a default response. He talks at a steady clip and often over-explains with work anecdotes. He uses 'mate' with men, says 'sort of' a lot and the odd 'er' when thinking. He tags sentences with 'you know' or 'right'. He fills silences himself rather than waiting, usually with a joke or 'anyway, yeah'. He is not bothered by awkwardness.
card.typing: Quick and careless. Mostly lowercase with no full stop at the end, and apostrophes often missed ('dont', 'its'). The occasional 'tbh' or 'lol'. Short answers like 'yeah fine' or 'not really bothered'. He doesn't reread before submitting, so the odd typo stays in.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and easy to talk to straight away, with a bit of a salesman's confidence. He jokes early and asks a couple of questions back, though he steers the conversation to his own stories. He comes across as likeable and unflappable, if a little pleased with himself, and he gets bored quickly if things get too abstract.
small_things: The dog ate a tea towel last week
Traffic on the M3 has been a nightmare with the roadworks
Thinking about getting a hot tub for the garden
His daughter's mocks are coming up
A rep took him out for a steak lunch
Got done by a speed camera on the A33 again
deeper_things: Being passed over for area manager two years ago still annoys him more than he lets on
His dad walked out when he was 14 and they barely speak; he doesn't feel much about it either way and says so
His mum is in a care home in Eastbourne, and he knows he doesn't visit as often as he should
He sometimes wonders whether he and Nicola have much to talk about once Ellie leaves home
Money's tighter than the car and holidays suggest, and he's put a bit more on credit cards than Nicola knows
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slightly low angle, so the camera looks up at him a little. He sits at a dining table, framed from mid-chest up, a bit off-centre to the left. He is a broad-faced white man with short, greying brown hair clipped at the sides and thinning on top, light stubble, and a slight sunburn on his nose and forehead. He wears no glasses. He has an easy half-smile and is looking just above the camera. He is wearing a navy quarter-zip fleet jumper with a small embroidered company logo on the chest. The lighting is evening ceiling light, warm and a bit flat, with some glare on his forehead. Behind him is an open-plan kitchen-diner: grey gloss kitchen units, a large black American-style fridge freezer with a calendar and takeaway menus held on by magnets, a kettle and a toaster on the worktop, a bowl with keys and a car fob in it, and a dog lead hanging off a cupboard handle. Part of a black Labrador's back is visible on a dog bed in the bottom right corner.
